Learned counsel for the applicant submits that during trial the prosecutrix was examined before the trial Court as PW-2 and at the time of cross-examination the counsel for the applicant cross-examined the prosecutirx and on 28.06.2022, the learned court below closed the opportunity of cross examination thereby holding that the counsel is asking irrelevant questions.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that thereafter the applicant moved a recall application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. for re-examination of PW-2 and the learned court below allowed the same on a cost of Rs. 600/- vide order dated 25.07.2022.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that thereafter the prosecutrix again appeared before the trial court and counsel for the applicant cross examined the prosecutrix and the counsel for the applicant asked specific question to the prosecutrix in regard to her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and against the learned trial court held that the counsel for the applicant is asking irrelevant questions and the trial court closed the opportunity of cross examinatio.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that on 10.08.2022 the applicant again moved an application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. for cross-examination of PW-2 and on the said application the complainant moved an objection on 14.09.2022 and stated that only for lingering on the case the applicant is moving the said applications and the trial Court vide impugned order dated 29.03.3024 rejected the same in an arbitrary manner.
Sri Arpit Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the argument advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and submits that the application filed on 10.08.2022 moved under Section 311 Cr.P.C. is the second application of the applicant with the intention only to delay the trial of the case.
On the first application of the applicant he was given chance but no relevant question were asked by the PW-2 and the trial court closed the opportunity of cross-examination.

The statement of the PW-2 was recorded and she appeared on four dates and around 15 pages statements were recorded and when on 28.06.2022 the applicant was given opportunity to cross-examine, the applicant's counsel used to ask irrelevant questions to the victim, thus the trial court rightly closed the opportunity to cross-examine PW-2.
On 25.07.2022 again the applicant was given time to cross-examine bu the applicant's counsel again asked the irrelevant question.
Thus the trial court has rightly close the opportunity to cross-examine the PW-2.
Learned A.G.A. for the State further submits that it is a ploy only to delay the trial.
The statement of the PW-2 has already been recorded.
No further statement is required to be taken by the victim or she should be cross-
examined by the applicant's counsel.
The trial Court by a detailed order has rightly rejected the application of the applicant and the case was fixed was evidence.
It was also argued by learned A.G.A. that the trial court may be directed to decide the trial expeditiously.

After considering the arguments as advanced by learned counsel for the parties and after perusal of the impugned order dated 29.03.2024, I do not find any illegality and infirmity in the impugned order.
The application filed by the applicant filed under Section 311 Cr.P.C. was rightly rejected.
This is ploy to delay the trial of the case, pending before the court below.
No case is made out.

In view of the aforesaid, I do not find any illegality or infirmity in the impugned order.
The present application lacks merit and is liable to be dismissed.
Dismissed accordingly.

The Trial Court may conclude the trial within six months from today without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties, unless there is some legal impediment or unless there is any order passed by the higher court staying the proceedings of the case.
Let a copy of this order be sent to the court concerned for its compliance.
